questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Time to overtake for uniform speed and constant acceleration from rest

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Time to overtake for uniform speed and constant acceleration from rest

hints: Set the displacement of the car equal to the displacement of the motorcycle: $s_{\text{car}} = 15t$ and $s_{\text{motorcycle}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)t^2 = 1.5t^2$.
Solve $1.5t^2 = 15t \implies 1.5t(t - 10) = 0 \implies t = 10\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write expressions for the displacements of both vehicles from the starting point:
$$s_{\text{car}} = 15t$$
$$s_{\text{motorcycle}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)t^2 = 1.5t^2$$

Equate the displacements to find the overtaking time:
$$1.5t^2 = 15t$$
$$1.5t(t - 10) = 0 \implies t = 10\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate kinematic equations:
- Constant velocity vehicle:
$$s_{\text{car}} = 15t$$
- Accelerating pursuer from rest:
$$s_{\text{motorcycle}} = 1.5t^2$$

Solve for intercept:
- Equating positions:
$$1.5t^2 - 15t = 0 \implies t = 10\text{ s}$$
The motorcycle overtakes the car after $10\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Equates displacements: $15t = \frac{1}{2}(3)t^2$.
Solves for non-zero root to obtain $t = 10\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 2: Speed of pursuer at the instant of overtaking

hints: Use the first equation of motion with initial speed zero: $v = at$.

walkthrough.text:
Apply $v = u + at$ for the motorcycle with $u = 0$, $a = 3\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$v = 0 + 3(10) = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Verify by checking that the average speed equals the constant speed of the car:
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{0 + 30}{2} = 15\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\text{This confirms the overtaking speed is } 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply velocity formula:
- Constant acceleration from rest:
$$v = a t$$

Evaluate speed at intercept:
- At $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$v = 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The motorcycle travels at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at the moment of overtaking.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$, $a = 3$, and $t = 10$.
Obtains speed $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Head-on meeting time between two bodies moving towards each other

hints: The two runners close the gap between them at a combined relative speed of $v_A + v_B = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Divide the initial separation by the relative speed: $t = \frac{180}{9} = 20\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the relative speed of approach between the two runners:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = v_A + v_B = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Calculate the time required to close the initial separation of $180\text{ m}$:
$$t = \frac{d}{v_{\text{rel}}} = \frac{180}{9} = 20\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine closure rate:
- Summing opposing speeds:
$$v_{\text{rel}} = 4 + 5 = 9\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Compute time of encounter:
- Time equals distance divided by closure rate:
$$t = \frac{180}{9} = 20\text{ s}$$
The runners meet after $20\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up total distance equation $(v_A + v_B)t = 180$.
Solves $(4 + 5)t = 180$ to obtain $t = 20\text{ s}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Time of minimum separation between two particles moving in the same direction

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Time of minimum separation between two particles moving in the same direction

hints: The separation distance between two bodies is stationary (minimum or maximum) when their velocities are equal: $v_B = v_A$.
Set $20 - 2t = 12 \implies 2t = 8 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the velocities of both particles at time $t$:
$$v_A = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v_B = 20 - 2t$$

Set $v_B = v_A$ to find the time of closest approach:
$$20 - 2t = 12$$
$$2t = 8 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Apply the relative velocity extremum rule:
- Minimum separation occurs when relative velocity is zero:
$$v_B(t) = v_A(t)$$

Solve for timestamp:
- Equating speeds:
$$20 - 2t = 12 \implies 2t = 8 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$$
The distance is minimum after $4\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies that minimum distance occurs when velocities match: $v_B = v_A$.
Solves $20 - 2t = 12$ to obtain $t = 4\text{ s}$.

$$t = \frac{50}{5} = 10\text{ s}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 6: Distance covered by accelerating pursuer before overtaking

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 6: Distance covered by accelerating pursuer before overtaking

hints: Let $t$ be the time cyclist $B$ has been moving. Displacements are $s_A = 4(t + 3)$ and $s_B = \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2 = t^2$.
Set $t^2 = 4t + 12 \implies t^2 - 4t - 12 = 0 \implies (t - 6)(t + 2) = 0 \implies t = 6\text{ s}$. Distance is $s = 6^2 = 36\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write the displacements of both cyclists where $t$ is the travel time of cyclist $B$:
$$s_A = 4(t + 3) = 4t + 12$$
$$s_B = \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2 = t^2$$

Equate the displacements and solve for $t$:
$$t^2 - 4t - 12 = 0 \implies (t - 6)(t + 2) = 0$$
$$\text{Taking the positive root } t = 6\text{ s}, \quad s = 6^2 = 36\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate quadratic intercept equation:
- Position equations:
$$t^2 = 4(t + 3) \implies t^2 - 4t - 12 = 0$$
$$(t - 6)(t + 2) = 0 \implies t = 6\text{ s}$$

Evaluate displacement:
- Position of either rider at $t = 6\text{ s}$:
$$s = 6^2 = 36\text{ m}$$
Cyclist $B$ overtakes Cyclist $A$ at a distance of $36\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up displacement equation $t^2 = 4(t + 3)$ and solves for positive root $t = 6\text{ s}$.
Calculates distance $s = 6^2 = 36\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 1: Police car pursuit with acceleration and constant maximum speed

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Police car pursuit with acceleration and constant maximum speed

hints: Time for police car to reach $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from rest is $t_1 = \frac{30}{3} = 10\text{ s}$. Distance covered is $s_{\text{police}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)(10^2) = 150\text{ m}$.
The speeding car has been moving for $10 + 2 = 12\text{ s}$, covering $s_{\text{car}} = 24(12) = 288\text{ m}$. Separation is $288 - 150 = 138\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Find the acceleration duration for the police car using $v = u + at$:
$$30 = 0 + 3t_1 \implies t_1 = \frac{30}{3} = 10\text{ s}$$

Calculate the displacement of each vehicle at $t = 10\text{ s}$ from the police car's start:
$$s_{\text{police}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)(10^2) = 150\text{ m}$$
$$s_{\text{car}} = 24(t_1 + 2) = 24(12) = 288\text{ m}$$

Find the separation distance between the two vehicles at this instant:
$$d = s_{\text{car}} - s_{\text{police}} = 288 - 150 = 138\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine acceleration time and displacement:
- Acceleration phase:
$$t_1 = \frac{30}{3} = 10\text{ s}$$
$$s_{\text{police}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)(100) = 150\text{ m}$$

Compute distance gap:
- Speeding car position (travelling for $12\text{ s}$):
$$s_{\text{car}} = 24 \times 12 = 288\text{ m}$$
- Separation:
$$d = 288 - 150 = 138\text{ m}$$
The police car reaches top speed after $10\text{ s}$, trailing by $138\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $v = at$ to find acceleration time: $t_1 = \frac{30}{3} = 10\text{ s}$.
Calculates displacements: $s_{\text{police}} = \frac{1}{2}(3)(100) = 150\text{ m}$ and $s_{\text{car}} = 24(10 + 2) = 288\text{ m}$.
Obtains separation distance $288 - 150 = 138\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 1: Police car pursuit with acceleration and constant maximum speed

hints: During the constant speed phase, the relative speed of approach is $30 - 24 = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Time to close the $138\text{ m}$ gap is $\frac{138}{6} = 23\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:

$$v_{\text{rel}} = 30 - 24 = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta t = \frac{138}{6} = 23\text{ s}$$

Calculate total elapsed time from the car's initial passage and total distance:
$$T_{\text{total}} = 2 + 10 + 23 = 35\text{ s}$$
$$s_{\text{total}} = 24 \times 35 = 840\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Check with police car: } 150 + 30(23) = 150 + 690 = 840\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine closure time at top speed:
- Gap closing rate is $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta t = \frac{138}{6} = 23\text{ s}$$

Compute total duration and distance:
- Total time since car passed checkpoint:
$$T = 2 + 10 + 23 = 35\text{ s}$$
- Distance travelled:
$$s = 24 \times 35 = 840\text{ m}$$
The police car overtakes after $35\text{ s}$ at a distance of $840\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets $150 + 30(t - 10) = 24(t + 2)$ to solve for $t = 33\text{ s}$ after pursuit began.
Obtains total time $33 + 2 = 35\text{ s}$ and total distance $24(35) = 840\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Head-on encounter between two accelerating and cruising vehicles

hints: At $t = 10\text{ s}$, combined distance is $100 + [96 + 24(2)] = 100 + 144 = 244\text{ m} < 464\text{ m}$.

For $t > 10\text{ s}$, both cars cruise: combined speed is $20 + 24 = 44\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Remaining gap is $464 - 244 = 220\text{ m}$. Time needed is $\frac{220}{44} = 5\text{ s}$, so $t = 10 + 5 = 15\text{ s}$. Distance from $P$ is $100 + 20(5) = 200\text{ m}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the positions of both cars at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$s_A(10) = 100\text{ m}$$
$$s_B(10) = 96 + 24(10 - 8) = 96 + 48 = 144\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Combined distance covered by } t = 10\text{ s} \text{ is } 100 + 144 = 244\text{ m}$$

Calculate the time to close the remaining gap of $464 - 244 = 220\text{ m}$ at constant cruising speeds:
$$v_{\text{combined}} = v_A + v_B = 20 + 24 = 44\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$\Delta t = \frac{220}{44} = 5\text{ s}$$
$$t = 10 + 5 = 15\text{ s}$$
$$s_A = 100 + 20(5) = 200\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate separation after initial acceleration:
- Gap remaining at $t = 10\text{ s}$:
$$d_{\text{rem}} = 464 - (100 + 144) = 220\text{ m}$$

Solve for meeting timestamp and location:
- Cruising closure duration:
$$\Delta t = \frac{220}{20 + 24} = 5\text{ s} \implies t = 15\text{ s}$$
- Distance from point $P$:
$$s_A = 100 + 20(5) = 200\text{ m}$$
The cars meet after $15\text{ s}$ at a distance of $200\text{ m}$ from $P$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up total distance equation for $t > 10$: $[100 + 20(t - 10)] + [96 + 24(t - 8)] = 464$.
Solves $44t - 196 = 464 \implies t = 15\text{ s}$, and finds distance from $P$ as $s_A(15) = 200\text{ m}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 3: Two-stage intercept and maximum lead between linear bodies

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Two-stage intercept and maximum lead between linear bodies

hints: Particle $A$ has been moving for $t + 4$ seconds when $B$ has been moving for $t$ seconds, so $s_A = 6(t + 4) = 6t + 24$.
Particle $B$ starts with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and decelerates at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$: $s_B = 20t - \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2 = 20t - t^2$.
Set $s_A = s_B \implies 20t - t^2 = 6t + 24 \implies t^2 - 14t + 24 = 0$.
Factor: $(t - 2)(t - 12) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 12\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Write expressions for the displacements of both particles from $O$ in terms of $t$:
$$s_A = 6(t + 4) = 6t + 24$$
$$s_B = 20t - \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2 = 20t - t^2$$

Equate the two displacements to find when the particles are at the same point:
$$20t - t^2 = 6t + 24$$
$$t^2 - 14t + 24 = 0$$

Factor the quadratic equation to determine the two encounter times:
$$(t - 2)(t - 12) = 0$$
$$t = 2\text{ s} \quad \text{and} \quad t = 12\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Formulate displacement functions:
- Constant speed body with $4\text{ s}$ head start:
$$s_A = 6(t + 4) = 6t + 24$$
- Decelerating particle from origin:
$$s_B = 20t - t^2$$

Solve quadratic crossing equation:
- Equating positions:
$$t^2 - 14t + 24 = 0 \implies (t - 2)(t - 12) = 0$$
The particles meet at $t = 2\text{ s}$ and again at $t = 12\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses displacements as $s_A = 6(t + 4) = 6t + 24$ and $s_B = 20t - t^2$.
Equates $s_A = s_B$ to form quadratic $t^2 - 14t + 24 = 0$.
Solves quadratic to obtain meeting times $t = 2\text{ s}$ and $t = 12\text{ s}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Two-stage intercept and maximum lead between linear bodies

hints: The lead of $B$ over $A$ is $D(t) = s_B - s_A = (20t - t^2) - (6t + 24) = -t^2 + 14t - 24$.
The lead is maximized when the rates of change of position match, so $v_B = v_A \implies 20 - 2t = 6 \implies 2t = 14 \implies t = 7\text{ s}$.
Notice that $t = 7\text{ s}$ is also the midpoint of the two encounter times: $\frac{2 + 12}{2} = 7\text{ s}$.

walkthrough.text:
Define the separation distance function representing the lead of $B$ over $A$:
$$D(t) = s_B - s_A = (20t - t^2) - (6t + 24) = -t^2 + 14t - 24$$

Find the maximum by equating velocities ($v_B = v_A$) or setting the derivative to zero:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}D}{\mathrm{d}t} = -2t + 14 = 0 \implies 2t = 14 \implies t = 7\text{ s}$$

Evaluate the maximum lead distance at $t = 7\text{ s}$:
$$D(7) = -(7^2) + 14(7) - 24 = -49 + 98 - 24 = 25\text{ m}$$
Alternatively, completing the square:
$$D(t) = 25 - (t - 7)^2 \implies D_{\max} = 25\text{ m} \text{ at } t = 7\text{ s}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate maximum separation:
- Velocity match criterion:
$$v_B = v_A \implies 20 - 2t = 6 \implies t = 7\text{ s}$$
(Equivalently, the vertex of the parabola lies midway between crossings at $t = 2$ and $t = 12$).

Evaluate maximum lead:
- Maximum value of quadratic:
$$D(7) = 25 - (7 - 7)^2 = 25\text{ m}$$
Particle $B$ achieves its maximum lead of $25\text{ m}$ at $t = 7\text{ s}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies that maximum lead occurs when speeds match ($v_B = v_A$), or completes the square on $D(t) = -t^2 + 14t - 24$.
Solves $20 - 2t = 6$ to obtain $t = 7\text{ s}$.
Evaluates maximum lead: $D(7) = 20(7) - 49 - (6(7) + 24) = 91 - 66 = 25\text{ m}$.

Calculate the total distance covered by Max across his three stages:
$$s_{1} = 18\text{ m}$$
$$s_{2} = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ m}$$
$$s_{3} = \frac{6 + 0}{2}(4) = 12\text{ m}$$
$$s_{\text{Max}} = 18 + 48 + 12 = 78\text{ m}$$

Express the total distance covered by Leo in terms of acceleration $a$:
$$v_{\max} = 4a$$
$$s_{\text{Leo}} = \frac{1}{2}(4)(4a) + 8(4a) + \frac{1}{2}(4)(4a) = 8a + 32a + 8a = 48a$$
$$\text{For } a = 1.5: \quad s_{\text{Leo}} = 48(1.5) = 72\text{ m}$$

Compare the distances:
$$\Delta s = s_{\text{Max}} - s_{\text{Leo}} = 78 - 72 = 6\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Max travels further by } 6\text{ m}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Evaluate Max's total track distance:
- Summing acceleration, cruising, and braking segments:
$$s_{\text{Max}} = 18 + 48 + 12 = 78\text{ m}$$

Evaluate Leo's total distance at $a = 1.5\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
- Peak velocity $v = 4(1.5) = 6\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$s_{\text{Leo}} = 48(1.5) = 72\text{ m}$$
Max travels further by $78 - 72 = 6\text{ m}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates total distance for Max: $s_{\text{Max}} = 18 + 6(8) + \frac{6}{2}(4) = 18 + 48 + 12 = 78\text{ m}$.
Calculates total distance for Leo in terms of $a$: $s_{\text{Leo}} = \frac{1}{2}(4a)(4) + 4a(8) + \frac{1}{2}(4a)(4) = 48a$.
Substitutes $a = 1.5$ to get $s_{\text{Leo}} = 72\text{ m}$ and concludes Max travels further by $6\text{ m}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 5: Two-stage acceleration and deceleration with minimum separation analysis

hints: Let $\tau = t - 8$ be the time into the deceleration phase. The speed of $Q$ is $v_Q = 16 - \tau$.
The distance between them is at a minimum when their speeds are equal: $16 - \tau = 12 \implies \tau = 4\text{ s}$, which corresponds to $t = 12\text{ s}$.
Calculate displacements at $t = 12\text{ s}$: $s_P(12) = 12(12) = 144\text{ m}$, and $s_Q(12) = 64 + 16(4) - \frac{1}{2}(1)(16) = 120\text{ m}$.
Minimum distance is $144 - 120 = 24\text{ m} > 0$, proving $Q$ never overtakes $P$.

walkthrough.text:
Analyze the deceleration phase ($\,t \ge 8\,$). Let $\tau = t - 8$ be the time elapsed since deceleration began:
$$v_Q(\tau) = 16 - 1\tau$$
Closest approach occurs when the velocities of both particles are equal:
$$v_Q(\tau) = v_P \implies 16 - \tau = 12 \implies \tau = 4\text{ s} \quad (t = 12\text{ s})$$

Calculate the displacements of both particles at $t = 12\text{ s}$ ($\tau = 4\text{ s}$):
$$s_P(12) = 12(12) = 144\text{ m}$$
$$s_Q(12) = 64 + 16(4) - \frac{1}{2}(1)(4^2) = 64 + 64 - 8 = 120\text{ m}$$

Calculate the minimum separation distance:
$$d_{\min} = s_P(12) - s_Q(12) = 144 - 120 = 24\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Because } d_{\min} = 24\text{ m} > 0, \text{ particle } Q \text{ never overtakes particle } P$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Locate point of closest approach:
- Velocity matching condition during braking:
$$16 - \tau = 12 \implies \tau = 4\text{ s} \implies t = 12\text{ s}$$

Evaluate minimum distance:
- Displacements at $t = 12\text{ s}$:
$$s_P = 144\text{ m}, \quad s_Q = 64 + 64 - 8 = 120\text{ m}$$
$$d_{\min} = 144 - 120 = 24\text{ m}$$
Because the minimum separation is strictly positive ($24\text{ m}$), $Q$ never overtakes $P$.

Obtains minimum distance $144 - 120 = 24\text{ m}$ and concludes $Q$ never overtakes $P$ since minimum separation is positive.

hints: Each stopping distance consists of reaction distance ($u \times 0.5$) plus braking distance ($\frac{u^2}{2a}$).
For Car $A$: reaction distance is $22(0.5) = 11\text{ m}$, braking distance is $\frac{22^2}{2(2)} = 121\text{ m}$. Total $s_A = 11 + 121 = 132\text{ m}$.
For Car $B$: reaction distance is $18(0.5) = 9\text{ m}$, braking distance is $\frac{18^2}{2(2)} = 81\text{ m}$. Total $s_B = 9 + 81 = 90\text{ m}$.
Sum: $132 + 90 = 222\text{ m}$. Since $222\text{ m} > 170\text{ m}$, the cars cannot stop before meeting.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the total stopping distance for Car $A$ (reaction plus braking):
$$s_{A, \text{react}} = 22(0.5) = 11\text{ m}$$
$$s_{A, \text{brake}} = \frac{22^2}{2(2)} = \frac{484}{4} = 121\text{ m}$$
$$s_{A, \text{total}} = 11 + 121 = 132\text{ m}$$

Calculate the total stopping distance for Car $B$ (reaction plus braking):
$$s_{B, \text{react}} = 18(0.5) = 9\text{ m}$$
$$s_{B, \text{brake}} = \frac{18^2}{2(2)} = \frac{324}{4} = 81\text{ m}$$
$$s_{B, \text{total}} = 9 + 81 = 90\text{ m}$$

Compare the combined stopping distance with the initial separation:
$$s_{\text{combined}} = 132 + 90 = 222\text{ m}$$
$$\text{Since } 222\text{ m} > 170\text{ m}, \text{ the cars cannot stop in time and a collision is inevitable}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute total stopping distances:
- Car $A$ requires:
$$s_A = 22(0.5) + \frac{22^2}{4} = 11 + 121 = 132\text{ m}$$
- Car $B$ requires:
$$s_B = 18(0.5) + \frac{18^2}{4} = 9 + 81 = 90\text{ m}$$

Assess collision condition:
- Combined stopping distance required:
$$132 + 90 = 222\text{ m} > 170\text{ m}$$
Because $222\text{ m}$ exceeds the available $170\text{ m}$ track separation, collision is inevitable.

hints: During the $0.5\text{ s}$ reaction phase, the cars travel $11 + 9 = 20\text{ m}$, leaving $170 - 20 = 150\text{ m}$ between them.
Let $\tau = t - 0.5$ be the braking duration. Displacements during braking: $s_A = 22\tau - \frac{1}{2}(2)\tau^2 = 22\tau - \tau^2$, and $s_B = 18\tau - \tau^2$.
Set combined braking distance to $150\text{ m}$: $40\tau - 2\tau^2 = 150 \implies \tau^2 - 20\tau + 75 = 0$.
Factor: $(\tau - 5)(\tau - 15) = 0$. The first collision occurs at $\tau = 5\text{ s}$, so total time is $t = 0.5 + 5 = 5.5\text{ s}$.
Calculate speeds at impact using $v = u - a\tau$: $v_A = 22 - 2(5) = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_B = 18 - 2(5) = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the remaining separation between the cars after the $0.5\text{ s}$ reaction time:
$$d_{\text{react}} = 11 + 9 = 20\text{ m}$$
$$d_{\text{rem}} = 170 - 20 = 150\text{ m}$$

Set up the combined displacement equation during the braking phase where $\tau = t - 0.5$:
$$s_A(\tau) + s_B(\tau) = (22\tau - \tau^2) + (18\tau - \tau^2) = 40\tau - 2\tau^2$$
$$40\tau - 2\tau^2 = 150 \implies 2\tau^2 - 40\tau + 150 = 0$$
$$\tau^2 - 20\tau + 75 = 0 \implies (\tau - 5)(\tau - 15) = 0$$

Select the physically valid root $\tau = 5\text{ s}$ and compute the total elapsed time and impact speeds:
$$t = 0.5 + 5 = 5.5\text{ s}$$
$$v_A = 22 - 2(5) = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v_B = 18 - 2(5) = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate distance after reaction delay:
- Road gap when braking begins:
$$d_{\text{rem}} = 170 - 20 = 150\text{ m}$$

Solve braking intercept quadratic:
- Combined deceleration equation:
$$\tau^2 - 20\tau + 75 = 0 \implies (\tau - 5)(\tau - 15) = 0$$
Braking lasts $\tau = 5\text{ s}$, giving total time $t = 5.5\text{ s}$.

Evaluate velocities at impact:
- Speeds just before collision:
$$v_A = 22 - 10 = 12\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
$$v_B = 18 - 10 = 8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The cars collide after $5.5\text{ s}$ at speeds of $12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
